data.scenario_text: A windshield wiper pivots through an angle of <m>140^\circ</m> and sweeps out a circular sector of the windshield with a radius of <m>24</m> inches.
data.length_task: The tip of the wiper blade travels along the outer arc of the region. To the nearest inch, how far does the tip travel in a single sweep?
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The region cleared by the wiper is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 24 inches, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 140^\circ, both straight sides 24 inches, and the arc s. For this situation the two straight sides are the wiper arm in its starting and ending positions, and the arc is the path swept out by the tip of the blade.

Part (b). The area of a sector is A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta, but that formula only works when the angle is measured in radians, so we convert the given angle first.

\theta = 140^\circ = 140^\circ \cdot \frac{\pi\ \text{rad}}{180^\circ} = \frac{7}{9} \, \pi\ \text{rad} \approx 2.4435\ \text{rad}

Now substitute r = 24 inches and \theta \approx 2.4435 radians into the area formula:

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(24\ \text{in})^2 \left(\frac{7}{9} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 703.72\ \text{in}^2

The auto detailer charges \$0.12 for every square inch, so we multiply the area by that rate. The square inch units cancel, leaving dollars:

\text{cost} = 703.72\ \text{in}^2 \cdot \frac{\$0.12}{1\ \text{in}^2} = \boxed{\$84.45}

So the total cost to treat the region cleared by the wiper is \boxed{\$84.45}.

Part (c). The arc is the curved outer edge of the region cleared by the wiper, and its length is s = r\theta, with \theta in radians (the same value we used in part (b)).

s = r\theta = (24\ \text{in})\left(\frac{7}{9} \, \pi\right) \approx \boxed{59.0\ \text{in}}

So the tip of the wiper blade travels about 59.0 inches in a single sweep.
